text: There were no showers… so 500 years ago, you could go months without a full bath. And you'd smell.
whisper: There were no showers, so 500 years ago, you could go months without a full bath, and you'd smell.

text: First, the river. Free… but freezing.
whisper: First, the river. Free but freezing.

text: Rome had public baths. No soap: you oiled your skin and scraped it off with a curved metal stick. This is a strigil. But the water wasn't always fresh.
whisper: Rome had public baths. No soap. You oiled your skin and scraped it off with a curved metal stick. This is a Strigil. But the water wasn't always fresh.

text: Medieval towns had steamy bathhouses called stews… with a bad reputation. In 1546, Henry the Eighth shut London's down.
whisper: Medieval towns had steamy bathhouses called stews, with a bad reputation. In 1546, Henry VIII shut London's down.

text: Doctors said hot water let disease in through the skin. So people wore a clean linen shirt to soak up the dirt… plus perfume. This is a dry wash.
whisper: Doctors said hot water let disease in through the skin, so people wore a clean linen shirt to soak up the dirt plus perfume. This is a dry wash.

text: Later, the tin tub, filled pot by pot… and the whole family shared the water. The story goes, the baby went last.
whisper: Later, the tin tub filled pot by pot and the whole family shared the water. The story goes, the baby went last.

text: In 1767, William Feetham patented a shower: pump water up by hand, pull a chain… and the same dirty water falls again.
whisper: In 1767, William Fetum patented a shower, pump water up by hand, pull a chain, and the same dirty water falls again.

text: Then came pipes and water heaters. Hot water, any time. This is a shower.
whisper: Then came pipes and water heaters, hot water any time, this is a shower!

text: Today, the average shower takes about eight minutes. Logging off.
whisper: Today, the average shower takes about 8 minutes logging off.
